thread_title: S. alata Nova #1 'Dark Lid' Stone Co, MS
breadcrumb: S. alata Nova #1 'Dark Lid' Stone Co, MS

posts.body_html:
is this an atrorubra? probably. Is MW calling it that just yet? No. Why? Because it would sound a bit cumbersome to say S. alata var. atrorubra Nova #1 'dark lid' Stone Co, MS every time someone asks about this clone in particular, let alone typing it or having voice to text screw up the words every time is just an absolute pain. Any questions? Didn't think so. LOL J/K

But MAY-AN! That's an over-exaggerated enunciation of the word MAN! Check out the dark lid on this baby! It's already january and the darn trap is still in decent shape even though 99% of the entire collection looks dead and brown right now for the dormancy period. This trap has literally weathered torrential rains, countless light freezes at night, and several nights below 28F. This goes to show, if you're trying to breed ever-green traps, this is one that I would tinker with. Not tinkle, right?
